name: CoreWeave
day_summary: CoreWeave is having a hard session — $100.88, down 4.58% (-$4.84) from a $105.72 prior close, trading $98.25–$104.54 on heavy 21.6M-share volume and probing the $100 round number. There was no fresh company headline; the slide is the same risk-off rotation out of high-multiple, cash-burning AI-infrastructure names that hit Nebius today, with capital favoring 'cheaper' AI plays after Micron's blowout. CRWV is now ~42% below its $173.35 52-week high even though the business keeps scaling: Q1 2026 revenue more than doubled to $2.08B, the contracted-power base is ~3.5GW, and the revenue backlog sits at a staggering $99.4B (OpenAI, Anthropic, and a $21B Meta deal among the anchors). The bears won the tape today; the debate is whether the de-rating is healthy or a warning on the debt-funded buildout model.
long_pnl: Longs from the lows ($63.80 52-week low) are still well ahead, but anyone who chased the $173 highs is down ~42% and took another 4.6% hit today; the name has spent 2026 giving back its post-IPO euphoria even as revenue compounds.
short_pnl: Shorts pressing the 'great business, broken stock' thesis had another green day — the failure at $104 and slide through $100 rewarded fading rallies in the most capital-intensive AI neocloud, though a $99.4B backlog makes the structural short a high-wire act.

decision.horizon: 1–2 quarters · into the Q2 2026 print (~early Aug) and proof the capex is being financed without crippling dilution
decision.rationale: HOLD at medium conviction — high-variance. CoreWeave is the largest pure-play AI neocloud: Q1 revenue $2.08B (+112% YoY), FY26 guidance of $12–13B, ~3.5GW of contracted power, and a $99.4B backlog anchored by OpenAI, Anthropic and a $21B Meta agreement. That is exactly the compute bottleneck our Situational Awareness desk argues the AI buildout runs into — and CRWV is one of Aschenbrenner's disclosed longs. But the model is brutally capital-hungry: a $740M quarterly net loss (widening), a $31–35B 2026 capex plan, and heavy reliance on debt and GPU-backed financing. The stock's ~42% drawdown from the highs is the market repricing that risk, not the demand. Own it small as the flagship neocloud, add on washouts toward the $90s/$80s, and treat the financing cadence — not the backlog — as the swing factor. This is a position sized for volatility, not conviction-maxed.

what_traders_are_doing: Treating CRWV as the high-beta sentiment proxy for the AI-compute buildout. Playbook: (1) respect the volatility — size for a ~75% IV name that can move ±5% with no news, as it did today; (2) the $100 round number is the line in the sand — a daily close below opens the $90s and a retest toward $80; holding it keeps the base intact; (3) the real catalyst is financing, not demand — watch how the $31–35B capex gets funded (debt, GPU-backed facilities, equity) and any commentary on free-cash-flow timing at the Q2 print; (4) pair-trade lens — CRWV and NBIS move together as the neocloud complex; divergence between them often signals a single-name financing story; (5) cross-reference /situational-awareness — CRWV is a disclosed Aschenbrenner long and a tell for the picks-and-shovels thesis.

outlook.short_term: Volatile and sentiment-driven, with $100 the pivotal level. With no company catalyst until the Q2 print, CRWV trades as a high-beta read on AI-infrastructure risk appetite and rate sensitivity. Expect wide swings; reclaiming $105–$110 signals the dip is bought, losing $98 opens the $90s.
outlook.long_term: Potentially one of the best-positioned AI neoclouds — a $99.4B backlog and 3.5GW of power are the literal scarce inputs of the AI era. But the long-term return depends entirely on financing a $31–35B-per-year buildout without diluting holders into the ground or over-levering against fast-depreciating GPUs. If CoreWeave converts the backlog to free cash flow before the balance sheet strains, the upside is large; if capital markets tighten, the model is fragile. High reward, real risk — a deliberately small, high-conviction sleeve.

analysis: CoreWeave is the purest, largest public bet on the AI-compute bottleneck — and the cleanest illustration of that bet's central tension. On one side: a $99.4B backlog, 3.5GW of contracted power, revenue doubling to $2.08B, and the frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) plus a $21B Meta deal as customers. On the other: a widening $740M quarterly loss and a $31–35B annual capex plan funded with debt against GPUs that depreciate on a hardware clock. The market spent 2026 repricing that second half, taking the stock ~42% off its highs, and today's -4.6% is more of the same risk-off rotation rather than a demand problem. For the copy-trade thesis our Situational Awareness desk tracks, CRWV is a core holding and a tell: it is exactly the picks-and-shovels exposure Aschenbrenner favors, expressed at the most capital-intensive end of the spectrum. Own it small, let $100 prove itself, add on washouts into the $90s/$80s, and judge the next leg on the financing path, not the backlog — the backlog is not the question.
